title: Introducing ChatGPT Wallet
notes: Read from the Internet Archive capture of 2026-11-13T16:04:07Z (archiveUrl) because openai.com answers 403 to automated reads; the RSS item is dated 2026-11-13T15:00:00Z. The capture says Wallet is built in partnership with American Express, Mastercard and Visa, will initially be available through dots for ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the US (aged 18 and older, with eligible US-issued cards) and begins rolling out that day. The user adds a card once; before each purchase the user reviews the items, total and selected card and approves with a security check such as Face ID or a fingerprint scan, and each approval creates a record of the authorized purchase. After approval the payment network provides a payment token with a card number, security code and expiration date, so neither the business nor the agent sees the actual card details; users keep card rewards and protections for eligible disputes, and businesses keep pricing, fulfillment, returns and customer service. It names fraud prevention partners including Forter, Riskified, Sardine and Signifyd and PSPs including Adyen, Checkout.com and Stripe (lists marked as not exhaustive), quotes American Express calling Wallet its first Agentic Commerce Experiences integration, announces the Commerce Partner Playbook at developers.openai.com/commerce, says risk systems may still decline legitimate agent purchases, and gives 1.2B weekly ChatGPT users. A future option to delegate purchases within spending limits, categories or time periods is described without a date. It states no fee and never mentions the Agentic Commerce Protocol, ACP, Instant Checkout, Delegate Payment or Shared Payment Tokens. The capture's meta, og and twitter descriptions, like OpenAI's RSS description of the same post (src-openai-news-rss-20261114), name agents in ChatGPT Work, Codex and dots; the post body names dots only.

title: Accept payments (Commerce in ChatGPT, OpenAI developer docs)
notes: Read through the .md twin (HTTP 200 at 2026-11-15T02:47Z UTC). Customers can pay with ChatGPT Wallet on the business's website or use a payment method already saved there, after approving in ChatGPT; the business handles the order, fulfillment, customer support and fraud decisions. Wallet works with existing checkout pages and payment forms, with no Wallet-specific integration. The merchant receives a network token instead of the card number and can use the Payment Account Reference (PAR) to link it to the account; the customer consents only to the specific transaction, so the credential must not be reused or saved for another purchase; subscriptions work if the checkout supports recurring billing, with the customer's consent and the processor's practice for merchant-initiated transactions; Wallet is a separate option beside an existing card-on-file flow. OpenAI says it is rolling out user signals in the Forwarded HTTP header with the parameters asn, for, ip-country, ip-prefix, locale, tz and user-agent, and that the signals may vary during the rollout. First archive capture of the page 2026-11-13T17:12:22Z.

title: Help ensure cloud browser access to your site (Commerce in ChatGPT, OpenAI developer docs)
notes: Read through the .md twin (2026-11-15T02:47Z and 03:04Z UTC). ChatGPT's cloud browser needs no allowlist. ChatGPT uses Web Bot Auth (RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signatures) to identify certain automated browser requests, and the guidance applies to signed cloud browser requests, not web crawlers: a signed request carries Signature and Signature-Input headers and a Signature-Agent header set to the quoted string https://chatgpt.com, and keys are published at https://chatgpt.com/.well-known/http-message-signatures-directory. Akamai, Cloudflare, HUMAN and Vercel verify the signatures automatically; other providers should verify signatures before applying an allowlist exception. FAQ: site owners cannot yet control which actions users take, but OpenAI requires human review before any consequential action across all users; browser access needs no product feed or plugin; OpenAI says customers are ultimately responsible for the actions they take, so support follows the business's normal process. The page does not say whether the signature covers the Forwarded header.

title: Build a plugin (Commerce in ChatGPT, OpenAI developer docs)
notes: Read through the .md twin (2026-11-15T02:47Z UTC). Recommends a headless MCP plugin and says iframe-based MCP UI is not supported in dots; the tool groups for product lookup, carts, checkout and order history (when supported) are examples, not mandatory tool names or a universal schema; product lookup and carts should work in guest mode; OpenAI supports mutual TLS for MCP servers; a plugin that cannot finish checkout returns a continue_url browser handoff, ideally a short-lived one-time authenticated link. Its reference checkout shape for create_checkout, get_checkout and update_checkout is described as following a cart and checkout proposal that the page does not name; its fields (item id, title and price; totals with only type and amount; a message with severity requires_buyer_input and a path; status requires_escalation) match UCP's checkout schema, not ACP 2026-04-17's. Its cart and product lookup examples are OpenAI's own. OpenAI says it is still working on interaction patterns between third-party plugins and ChatGPT Wallet.

title: RFC 7239: Forwarded HTTP Extension
notes: Section 5.5 says extension parameters SHOULD be registered in the HTTP Forwarded Parameter registry; section 8.1 says the header cannot be relied on to be correct because any node on the way, including the client, may modify it.

ACP 2026-04-17 (commit 7fdd78d) instead has Item with id, name and unit_amount, MessageError severity info, low, medium, high or critical with separate resolution values and a param locator, and a Total that requires display_text.

title: Position of the Council at first reading on the Payment Services Regulation (ST 8543/1/26 REV 1)
notes: Dated 2026-11-04 (Brussels) and marked adopted by the Council on 2026-10-29 (procedure 2023/0210(COD)). No AI-agent provision: no hit for agentic, AI agent or autonomous. Recital 170: a pass-through wallet operator that verifies strong customer authentication needs an outsourcing agreement with the payer's PSP, which keeps full liability for the operator's failures to apply it; recitals 16 and 171: technical service providers and payment scheme operators are liable, up to the transaction amount, for failing to support strong customer authentication. Entry into force 20 days after publication, application 21 months later (Article 124). The Legislative Observatory lists the file as awaiting Parliament's second reading, with an indicative plenary date of 2026-12-14 (read 2026-11-14).

title: Position of the Council at first reading on the third Payment Services Directive (ST 8535/1/26 REV 1)

title: OCC Bulletin 2026-54, Super Intelligence: Supervisory Framework

The guidance says a business is responsible for what its AI agent does, as it is for an employee, even when someone else built or provides the agent, under the DMCC Act 2024, the Consumer Rights Act 2015 and the Consumer Contracts Regulations 2013.
